examples.problem:
$$
\mathbf{f}(t,z) = \big\langle \text{_____}, \: 4\sin{t}, \: z \big\rangle
$$

The vector-valued function $\mathbf{f}(t,z)$ above parametrizes the elliptic cylinder defined in Cartesian coordinates as $\dfrac{x^2}{4}+\dfrac{y^2}{16}=1.$ What is the first component of $\mathbf{f}?$
examples.worked_solution:
Recall that the ellipse $\dfrac{x^2}{4}+\dfrac{y^2}{16}=1$ in $xy$-plane has the parametrization

$$
\langle x,y \rangle = \big\langle 2\cos{t}, \: 4\sin{t} \big\rangle,
\qquad t \in [0,2\pi),
$$

since 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{16} & =\frac{(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}}{4}+\frac{(4\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}}{16} \\  & =\frac{4{cos}^{2}⁡t}{4}+\frac{16{sin}^{2}⁡t}{16} \\  & ={cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t,z) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,4\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,z⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $t \in [0,2\pi)$ and $z \in (-\infty,\infty).$

Therefore, the first component of $\mathbf{f}$ is ${\color{blue}2\cos{t}}.$

feedback.problem:
$$
f(y,z)=⟨\text{___},\,y,\,z⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $f(y,z)$ above parametrizes the parabolic cylinder defined in Cartesian coordinates as $x=3{y}^{2}.$ What is the first component of $f?$
feedback.worked_solution:
For any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(y,z) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨3{y}^{2},\,y,\,z⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $y\in (-\infty ,\infty )$ and $z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Therefore, the first component of $f$ is $3{y}^{2}.$
